items.title: NEW — the language server DIES with the analyzer: B385's stack overflow (SIGABRT in a check) took the whole `vilan-lsp` process down and the client restarted it, losing every open document's state; an analyzer abort should be CONTAINED per request — run the check on a thread with a large stack (or `catch_unwind` for panics; a stack overflow is not a panic and needs the thread), answer the request with an internal-error diagnostic naming the file, and keep serving
items.discussion: the owner (2026-09-22, ruled an item is wanted); B385 (the crash, fixed); N-class: robustness of `vilan-lsp`
items.status: OPEN — filed 2026-09-22 (the owner's ruling after B385)
items.body: Pins: a planted `unreachable!()` in a check answers a diagnostic and the NEXT request still works; a planted deep recursion (the B385 shape with the guard removed under a test flag) does the same via the stack-sized thread; `vilan-ide`'s tests (N115) get the twin. Rec: the check runs on a `std::thread::Builder::new().stack_size(..)` worker with `catch_unwind` around the analyzer call; a thread that dies by overflow is observed by `join`'s `Err`. Sizing S.
